topic: The Fundamental Bridge: Connecting Derivatives and Integrals

sections.title: The Hook: Speed vs. Distance
lecture_lines: A robot runs: speed is the instantaneous derivative.
Area under the speed curve is total distance.
These processes are inversely connected, remarkably.
animations: Show two cars (red A, blue B) at #FF0000 and #0000FF.
Animate cars moving across screen left to right.
Highlight yellow area (#FFFF00) under car B's speed path.
Display 'Distance is Area under Curve' in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Review of Prerequisite: The Derivative as a 'Zoom'
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.
Imagine zooming into a curve to see slope.
Slope defines the rate at that specific moment.
animations: Plot y=x^2 in white (#FFFFFF) on coordinate plane. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magnifyingglass.svg]
Create red (#FF0000) point moving along the curve.
Zoom in on point until curve looks like line.
Label slope 'dy/dx' in green (#00FF00) near tangent. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magnifyingglass.svg]

sections.title: The Integral as 'Summation'
lecture_lines: Integrals accumulate many tiny slices into one sum.
Think of filling a tank over time.
Adding these slices gives the total amount.
animations: Draw multiple thin rectangles (blue #0000FF) filling area [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg].
Sum areas of all rectangles to fill total [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg].

sections.title: The Fundamental Bridge
lecture_lines: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations.
They work like adding and subtracting numbers.
One builds up, the other breaks down.
F of x differentiated becomes f of x.
F of x integrated returns to original form.
animations: Show velocity v(t) curve in blue (#0000FF) with speedometer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg].
Show area growing as accumulation of velocity (yellow #FFFF00).
Demonstrate ∫[v(t)dt] = s(t) relationship using the speedometer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg].

sections.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: The Integral recovers the original anti-derivative.
Solve complex physics using this inverse relationship.
Fuel rate leads to exact rocket altitude.
animations: Draw plot showing rocket [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rocket.svg] fuel [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fuel.svg] consumption rate.
Fill area under curve (blue #0000FF) to show altitude.
